text:
sam: FYI we started seeing a perf regression on the KV-cache heavy workloads after the infra team rolled drivers yesterday. Traces look weird.
alisha: which driver/version? any nsys changes too?
sam: host was bumped to NVIDIA driver 535.104 and nsys on the perf VM is 2024.1. I pulled an nsys trace and saw CUPTI metric collection failing intermittently.
sam: snippet from nsys run: ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn --output=run1 nodelay_workload``` and then stderr had repeated `cuptiActivityEnable failed: CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED` lines.
mike: oof. `CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED` usually means version mismatch between CUPTI lib and driver or cupti not found in LD_LIBRARY_PATH in the container.
dan: we run these in a rootless container with seccomp+no new privs. Could be permissions blocking CUPTI attach.
lenka: can you paste the timeline? are kernels showing odd timestamp gaps or duplicated launches?
sam: timeline shows tiny kernels (kernel_a / kernel_b) launching many times instead of being batched. Example: kernel_a 3-7us then kernel_b 2us, a lot of host overhead. Before upgrade we had host-side batching and aggregated kernel durations 10-20x larger. The batcher heuristic now appears to believe kernels are short and refrains from merging.
alisha: so if CUPTI isn't producing correct activity records then the heuristic that estimates runtime cost and KV cache hit patterns may be undercounting effective sequence lengths.
sam: exactly. When CUPTI misses activities we treat kernels as cheaper -> smaller batch sizes -> more kernel launches -> extra KV cache churn -> regression.
mike: I also saw an nvprof vs nsys mismatch on a different host where timestamps drifted by microseconds after driver 535 series. Could be clock source change in driver -> ordering issues.
dan: infra-bot ran a quick check and found that container seccomp blocked `/proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid` reads for our profiling user. infra-bot: "seccomp rule: deny ptrace, deny perf_event_open for unprivileged".
lenka: quick workaround: run the profiler outside the container or enable a debug cap. For experiments I ran with `--cap-add=SYS_ADMIN` and CUPTI attached fine.
sam: confirmed: with SYS_ADMIN cap trace is complete and batching heuristic reverts to previous behavior, throughput back to baseline.
alisha: long term we need either: (1) coordinate with infra to allow CUPTI attach in rootless setups via a narrow cap, (2) package a lightweight tracing helper in the runtime that uses host-agent to collect activity, or (3) pin nsys/CUPTI version that is compatible with driver.
mike: adding version matrix note: nsys 2024.1 pairs with CUDA 12.4 / CUPTI 12.4. The driver 535.* is newer and sometimes ships with alternate runtime symbols; we've seen `cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks` return odd errors when the userland cupti is older/newer than kernel driver.
dan: created an infra ticket (INFRA-1102) to test: (a) repro with seccomp profile turned off, (b) test nsys 2023.6 vs 2024.1, (c) downgrade driver to 525.x in a canary.
lenka: also note: in the trace we saw `nvtx` marks but no activity for the launches between them which points at CUPTI underrun rather than lost GPU work.
sam: actionable: 1) run `ldd $(which nsys)` inside container and verify cupti lib loaded, 2) capture `dmesg` / container audit logs for denied syscalls, 3) re-run nsys with `--capture-range=nvtx` to isolate the gap.
alisha: FYI I created a small script `tools/check_cupti_attach.sh` that 1) ensures `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` has matching cupti, 2) runs a tiny CUDA kernel and validates `cuptiActivityEnable` success. Ping me and I'll drop it in CI.
mike: follow ups: add a runtime probe that validates CUPTI attach on startup and emits a warning to Console if sampling is not available. That should prevent silent regressions.
sam: thanks all. I'll attach the full `nsys` output and kernel timeline in the ticket. For now rolling back the driver on the perf VMs to 525.85 in canary and re-run baseline.
infra-bot: deploy job started: roll-driver/canary -> target perf-vm-03. ETA ~ 12m :hourglass:
lenka: small note for the batching heuristics team: make the heuristic resilient to missing CUPTI by falling back to kernel-duration estimates aggregated across host-observed submissions, and add a confidence score when activity metrics are sparse.
sam: adding that to the ticket. I'll update once canary completes or if we find a less disruptive fix.
